active_scope: Prompt 22 completed Go support. The decisive defect was environmental, not in the task code: the plans pointed GOCACHE/GOMODCACHE/GOPATH at /opt/pcb/cache inside the image, but the sandbox runs each guest with --read-only as an unprivileged uid that owns only /workspace and /tmp, so go build exited 2 with 'failed to initialize build cache ... read-only file system'. Exit 2 is a declared TOOL_ERRORS code, so the supervisor correctly classified it as a harness error and all six variants reported 'build:build harness error (tool_error)'. The asymmetry in the failed report is the proof: gofmt and context were measured because they need no build cache, while vet, staticcheck and gosec - which load packages through the cache - were all missing. Fixed by moving all four Go cache paths under the workspace tmpfs (GOTMPDIR included: /tmp is capped at 16 MiB and an ENOSPC there is indistinguishable from a candidate build error), and by having the guest runner create them because Go requires GOTMPDIR to exist. Three further defects fixed: the performance recipe's distinctness gate demanded a missing race detector that the pinned base always ships (now a declared per-recipe instrumentation contract with reciprocal release/instrumented guards, mirroring the C sanitizer arrangement); Go's hidden tests live in the package directory, which the shared admission engine hardcoded against (now an overlay_roots/overlay_suffixes plugin hint); and the Go image build did not refresh the allowlist, so a rebuild left every Go plan unrunnable. Images rebuilt, manifest resealed, allowlist verified against all five language identity files.
